title.en: The monsoon and seasons of India

text.en:
After a hot, dry summer the sky darkened and the first drops of rain fell on Latha's village. Farmers cheered and children ran outside.
"The monsoon has come!" shouted her grandfather. "Now our fields will turn green."

India has a tropical monsoon climate. The year can be divided into summer, the rainy season (monsoon), autumn or retreating monsoon, and winter.
The southwest monsoon winds bring moist air from the Indian Ocean and give most of India its rain from June to September. The northeast monsoon brings rain to Tamil Nadu in October and November.
The monsoon is important for farming, drinking water and rivers. Too little rain causes drought and too much causes floods. India's climate varies between regions: the north is cold in winter, the coast is humid and the desert is dry.
India has summer, a rainy season, a retreating monsoon and winter.
Southwest monsoon winds bring rain from June to September.
Tamil Nadu gets much of its rain from the northeast monsoon in October and November.
Too little rain causes drought. Too much causes floods.

problem.en: Why is the monsoon so important to Indian farmers?

text.en: Most crops need water, and much of India's farming depends on rain.
The monsoon gives most of the rain in just a few months.
If it fails, crops suffer; so farmers watch the monsoon closely.

prompt.en: A friend says it rains in Tamil Nadu mainly in June. How will you correct this?

requiredIdeas.en: Tamil Nadu gets much of its rain in October and November from the northeast monsoon.
June to September is the southwest monsoon for most of India.

commonMisconceptions.en: Assuming one monsoon for all regions.

points.en: India has a monsoon climate with four seasons.
The southwest monsoon brings rain from June to September.
Tamil Nadu gets rain from the northeast monsoon.
